question_text: How does graphite function as a lubricant?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The layers and the forces
lines: Graphite is built of flat sheets of
carbon atoms lying one above the other.
Within a sheet the carbon atoms are
Between one sheet and the next there
are only weak van der Waals forces.
steps.why: A lubricant works by putting a layer between two surfaces that moves easily under a sideways push. In graphite that easy movement happens between the sheets, so the answer has to name the sheets and the weak forces holding them together.
common_mistakes: Writing that the bonds inside a sheet are weak. Inside a sheet the covalent bonds are strong; it is the forces between the sheets that are weak.
Naming hydrogen bonds between the layers. Graphite is pure carbon; the forces between the sheets are van der Waals forces.
steps.memory_tip: Strong inside a sheet, weak between the sheets.
steps.margin_note: Describe the sheets and name the weak forces between them before giving the reason.

steps.label: The sliding
lines: Because the forces between the sheets
are weak, one sheet slides over the
next when a small sideways force is

Graphite is therefore soft and greasy,

moving surfaces lets them slide past

lines.text: The layers slide, so graphite lubricates

steps.why: The sliding is the whole mechanism. Because only the weak forces between the sheets are overcome and the sheets themselves stay whole, a film of graphite lasts instead of wearing away quickly.
common_mistakes: Stopping at soft and greasy without saying why. The sliding of the layers is the reason, and it has to be written.
Giving the delocalised electron as the reason. That electron explains why graphite conducts, not why it lubricates.
steps.memory_tip: Weak forces between layers means the layers slide, and sliding lubricates.
steps.margin_note: Finish with the word lubricant and say plainly what slides over what.

insider_note: A complete answer names the weak van der Waals forces between the sheets and says the sheets slide over one another, which is what makes graphite a lubricant.
